verdict: Caution: lend selectively to re-rollers with own scrap linkage and power backup; avoid single-mill, merchant-scrap-dependent units until pollution and power costs are verified.
title: Ghaziabad steel re-rolling & TMT: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
A Ghaziabad re-roller buys iron scrap, melts or heats it, rolls billets into TMT bars, and sells to local builders and stockists. **Cash is made in the spread between scrap-in and rebar-out, not in volume.** Scrap is quoted at ₹37.48/kg in Ghaziabad [1], so when a proposal lands, check the unit's scrap purchase rate against this local print; if their landed cost is materially above it, ask who their supplier is and why.

## Where value and cash sit
**Value sits in brand premium and power cost; cash sits in inventory days and debtor quality.** Branded TMT commands a premium over market rate [9], so ask for the brand's price differential and dealer list. Working capital is the real risk: peers carry moderately high working-capital needs supported by bank lines [11], and one peer's gearing deteriorated to 1.80x from 1.40x on debt-funded acquisition and higher working-capital borrowings [10]. So when a proposal lands, check inventory days and creditor days; if debtor days exceed creditor days by a wide gap, ask for the ageing and the top five buyers.

## What has changed now
**The local tailwind is real but thin.** UP GST collections grew 14.2% Apr-to-date versus India's 6.1% [D], yet UP electricity demand grew 8.6% versus India's 9.5% [D] — neutral for power-intensive rolling. India-wide IIP for NIC 24 rose 2.4% YoY and 3.4% Apr-to-date [D]. Peer results are strong: Steel Exchange India posted ~₹340 crore Q2 FY27 revenue, up ~45% YoY [6], and Rathi Steel crossed ₹200 crore, up over 30% YoY [7]. **But local news is thin and one item is a pollution notice to a factory near the RTO office [2]; treat that as a compliance signal, not a demand signal.** The ICRA MITC note is from March 2024 [8] and the Captain Steel note from February 2023 [9] — both old; use them for structure, not current pricing.

## Who to pursue now
**Pursue re-rollers with captive scrap sourcing, own or contracted power, and a branded TMT line.** These capture the brand premium [9] and survive scrap swings. **Avoid merchant-scrap-only single-mill units and any unit under a pollution notice [2] until consent is restored.** For the good ones, structure as a cash-flow term loan with a working-capital limit sized to inventory plus debtor days, not to turnover.

## How to grow safely and what to watch
**Take stock and debtor statements every month, plus GST returns and electricity bills.** If monthly GST payment falls below the trailing three-month average, ask for the sales register. If electricity units consumed drop sharply without a stated shutdown, ask for the production log. If scrap purchase rate moves more than a few percent from the ₹37.48/kg local print [1], re-check the spread. If any pollution notice [2] escalates to closure, freeze fresh disbursement.
